record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: What computational tools and modeling paradigms can implement and run simulations of self-modifying open systems whose programs, operators, structures, rules, or representational categories can evolve rather than remain fixed?

evidence.quote:
What are effective tools and modelling paradigms for implementing and running
(simulations of) self-modifying open systems?

Self-referential systems are natural in computing; self-modifying ones less so, but not unknown. Com-
puter science gives us tools for modelling, simulating, and analysing such systems; a few approaches are
summarised here.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning formal frameworks for simulating systems whose own programs, rules, and representational categories evolve. Existing tools (reflective interpreters, graph rewriting, P-systems, evolving algebras/ASMs, coalgebraic and categorical models of open systems) address fragments, but no single accepted framework satisfies all requirements; the problem is regarded as open in the literature on self-modifying and reflective computation.

status_evidence.title: Abstract State Machines / Evolving Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: ASMs model algorithms whose signatures and rules may be updated at runtime, providing partial support for self-modifying semantics.
status_evidence.claim: Existing paradigms only partially address self-modification of structure and rules.

status_evidence.title: Reflective computation (3-Lisp, metacircular interpreters)
status_evidence.snippet: Reflective systems can inspect and modify their own programs but typically keep a fixed representational substrate.
status_evidence.claim: Self-reference is supported but full evolution of representational categories is not standard.
